q: How do I calculate the carbon footprint of an air cooler?
title: Air cooler carbon footprint per unit
short: Weigh the plastic body, fan motor, pump, cooling pads and packaging, apply supplier or database factors, and add moulding and assembly electricity per unit. Report use-phase electricity separately; over a cooler's life it is usually larger than the making.

ul: Polypropylene or HIPS body: often the heaviest part; use a resin factor.
Fan motor and water pump: copper and steel.
Honeycomb or wood wool pads, castors, louvres and the carton.
Large injection moulding machines for tanks and bodies.
If you buy moulded bodies, the moulder's energy is their footprint; ask for it.

p: A cooler drawing about 150 to 200 W, run many hours in summer, uses a meaningful amount of electricity each year. State wattage, hours and grid factor.

example.title: Worked example: cooler plant per unit (one month)
lines: Plant total: 42,600 / 8,000 = 5.33 kg CO2 per cooler
Add plastic, motor, pump and pads for the full figure
example.note: Inputs are illustrative; use your own bills and production records.

senseible: Senseible reads the plant's electricity bills (CEA grid factor 0.710 kg CO2 per kWh, CO2 Baseline Database version 21.0) and fuel invoices (IPCC 2006 defaults) into a fingerprinted Scope 1 and 2 record, the plant-level input to a per-unit figure. Bought-in materials go to the supplier evidence trail; product reports are self-declared drafts.
